tier_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
tier_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
tier_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ck.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

It is an ordinary Collaboration Realm at the envelope level, but reducers MUST treat fields.purpose=principal_control + this schema_ref as an allowlist-bound control stream, not as a user collaboration space.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand ck.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 MUST treat the Realm as an ordinary Collaboration Realm and MUST NOT accept device/session/cross-signing state from it as principal control state.

binding_invariants: realm_id MUST equal the principal_control_realm_id resolved for the principal DID.
fields.purpose MUST be principal_control and schema_refs MUST contain ck.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.
Control events MUST bind principal_id / device_id / session grant audience to the same principal DID or an explicitly trusted recovery/session issuer.

ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ck.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / ck.realm.policy_components writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ck.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ck.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window

ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

ck.profile.auth_server.v1.description: Cokret v1 Auth Server profile. Auth Servers verify login factors (password / passkey / OIDC / SSO / recovery), issue short-lived audience-bound `ck.session.grant` artefacts, expose session-grant introspection / revocation, and MAY surface a `ck.self.policy.check` decision endpoint. ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ck.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Flow id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. additional_requirements.device_opt_in_must: Each receiving device MUST record an opt-in flag in its authorization state; absent opt-in, sender / Realm service MUST fall back to blind wakeup.
additional_requirements.ui_disclosure_must: Client UI MUST clearly indicate visible notification is active to the user.
additional_requirements.payload_minimisation_must: Even when claimed, payload MUST NOT carry message body, DID URLs, cross-Realm stable correlation keys, IP / geolocation, or untyped free-form text.

Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1 and zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §11.

additional_requirements.interop_only_must: This profile is interop-only; it MUST NOT be used as a substitute for ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 in default Cokret deployments.

ck.profile.media_service_binding.v1.description: Transport-agnostic media backend binding framework (CKP-0010). Requires ck.realm.media_service to declare a multi-focus list with backend type discriminator; defines normative token exchange, session focus selection, participant binding, E2EE key injection via MLS-Exporter label ck-rtc-frame-key/v1, and recording artifact pipeline. Specific backends (livekit / cokret-native) declare an additional sub-profile. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §2 / §3 / §5–§8 and zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §4.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed with unknown_focus_type for unsupported foci[].type values; MUST NOT infer a focus when foci[] is missing

additional_requirements.token_ttl_must: Token issuer MUST cap backend_token / participant_binding expires_at at 600s after issuance; SHOULD use ≤ 300s.
additional_requirements.issuer_did_anchoring_must: service_signature.kid and participant_binding.issuer_kid MUST resolve to a service DID declared in ck.realm.media_service.service_id of the current MLS epoch; otherwise reject with token_issuer_unauthorised.
additional_requirements.session_focus_must: ck.call.state.session_focus is write-once per call; in-session focus migration is not supported in v1. Token issuer MUST reject focus_id != committed session_focus (focus_mismatch).
additional_requirements.participant_binding_must: ck.call.state.participants[].participant_binding MUST be verified by both reducer (on event acceptance) and client (on backend ParticipantConnected event). Failure surfaces as participant_binding_invalid (reducer) or participant_identity_unrecognised (client).
additional_requirements.e2ee_key_source_must: Client binding adapter MUST derive frame keys from Cokret MLS-Exporter with label ck-rtc-frame-key/v1 (length=19 bytes, Context=canonical_json({realm_id, call_id, focus_id, epoch_id, participant_identity, device_id}), KDF.Nh=32 bytes), where participant_identity/device_id come from the verified ck.call.state.participants[] and participant_binding. Empty Context, missing sender fields, or epoch-only binding MUST be rejected with e2ee_key_source_unauthorised. MUST NOT accept keys from backend cloud key escrow; reject with e2ee_key_source_unauthorised.
additional_requirements.recording_pipeline_must: Backend-generated recording artifacts MUST flow through Cokret authenticated blob upload (media-and-blob.md) with recording_initiator_capability_ref. Direct backend-to-storage paths are forbidden (recording_artifact_pipeline_bypassed).
additional_requirements.recording_key_source_must: Recording artifact encryption keys MUST derive from Cokret MLS-Exporter label ck-rtc-recording-key/v1 with Context=canonical_json({realm_id, call_id, focus_id, recording_id, media_service_did, recording_start_event_id}) and 32 output bytes. The SFrame label ck-rtc-frame-key/v1 and empty Context MUST be rejected for recording artifacts.

ck.profile.media_service_binding.livekit.description: LiveKit backend binding sub-profile (CKP-0010 §4.5). Maps Cokret token_exchange to LiveKit JWT claims, SFrame-based E2EE via inject_frame_key, capability mapping to video.canPublishSources, and Egress-based recording through Cokret blob pipeline. Declaring this sub-profile requires declaring ck.profile.media_service_binding.v1. Optional in v1 cycle; not part of v1 mandatory conformance set. See zh/crypto-media/bindings/livekit.md.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; do not fall back to a non-production binding. Deployments needing an alternate backend MUST declare another production-grade media_service_binding sub-profile.

additional_requirements.livekit_metadata_ban_must: Token issuer MUST NOT inject LiveKit metadata or canUpdateOwnMetadata claims; Cokret participant metadata flows through ck.call.state only.
additional_requirements.livekit_recorder_claim_must: Token issuer MUST set video.recorder=false; recording goes through Cokret Egress proxy, not LiveKit recorder claim.

Declaring this sub-profile requires declaring ck.profile.media_service_binding.v1. See zh/crypto-media/bindings/cokret-native.md.

Declares wire-shape parity for the Matrix-derived surfaces: to-device queue, /keys/upload|query|claim, push gateway facade, cross-signing key hierarchy, SAS verification message flow. These bare names are not v1 wire Event.kind values. The action remains in the canonical capability registry so prose can reference it stably, but receivers that do not implement this profile MUST treat `ck.realm.join.review` as unknown (capability-action-registry.json registry_rules: 'Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default)'). Claiming the profile commits the implementation to the candidate join-policy workflow surface defined in zh/governance/join-policy.md. ck.profile.circle_anchor_cadence.fixed_5.description: Named cadence profile for confidential Circle sub-anchor commitments. Implementations claiming this profile MUST emit ck.circle.anchor_commit on a fixed time cadence (5 minutes, max jitter 30 seconds), MUST include empty-batch commitments, and MUST NOT use event-count or activity-triggered public commitments. Mobile energy saving may batch private sub-anchor upload, but MUST NOT relax the public Realm anchor cadence.

period_ms.rationale: Public Realm anchor commitment cadence is fixed at 5 minutes for this profile.

max_jitter_ms.rationale: Bounded scheduling jitter; implementations MUST NOT encode activity by delaying beyond this window.

empty_batch_commitments.rationale: No-activity intervals still emit commitments to avoid leaking activity frequency.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; confidential Circle deployments MUST NOT claim an event-count cadence as equivalent

ck.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept ck.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor ck.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `ck.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor ck.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: fail closed or omit profile claim

ck.profile.circle_conformance.v1.description: Conformance profile pinning the machine-contract surface for Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md). Splits actor submit-payload (scope_circle_id only) from canonical reducer-output (tagged effective_scope on Event envelope + materialized object), and pins the Circle event-kind family, member-state transition table, encryption-profile compatibility, and scope-rebind reducer-reject semantics. Required by implementations that emit or consume Circle events or that materialize Circle-scoped Flow / Message / Morph / Relation / Space objects.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: implementations that cannot enforce canonical reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST NOT claim ck.profile.circle_conformance.v1; receivers MUST treat any unknown Circle event-kind as schema_violation

additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Submit payload for ck.flow.create / ck.message.create / ck.morph.create / ck.relation.create / ck.space.create / ck.space.parent MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). Reducer MUST reject any submit payload that also carries effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: Reducer MUST stamp tagged effective_scope on accepted Event envelope and materialized object cell. effective_scope is immutable per-event; later scope_circle_id rebinds MUST NOT re-interpret historical events.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ck.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ck.realm.policy_components or ck.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ck.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ck.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver events with effective_scope.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).
